items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I actually interviewed him for the book up at the, I think it was up above the Apollo Theater... And then another day was backstage at the Strand Theatre... so I went backstage and got to talk to him quite a while

ctx.x: I'm going to ask a real killer of a question. How did you ever get interested in jazz?

Well, I heard music when I was a kid, of course, like on the river boats and other places around town. I was raised in a small town on the Mississippi River. There wasn't any real jazz bands, but there used to be a few piano players, and especially on the boats I'd hear jazz. But I didn't really try to listen to it. I used to have the idea that it was... In fact, my violin teacher told me, don't try to play any of that music. It'll, you know, corrupt your style. I'll revile it. So, I did listen to records,…
Where'd you get, where would you get?

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: Once at the Blue Note in Chicago, Louis was playing a German horn... And he made the remark to me... I might have asked him something about the Selmer

ctx.x: Well, you could tell me how American music got started. It started at the beginning.

So anyway, to get back to the point, Gene Williams had heard these records and agreed with me too that at least Bunk showed some possibilities. You couldn't really tell much how he played, both because his lip wasn't in shape and just by himself. The type of trumpet playing that Bunk did, which was a remarkable thing, and yet by itself it wouldn't sound that effective. Bunk was hardly ever on the beat, so if you didn't hear him patting his foot and all there, you could really tell of course where the beat is, but…

1949. It says here she was approximately later, 11 years older than George Bakke. I figured that out. To get on to a few other people that I used to talk to, the next one on this list was Johnny Dodds, whose notes I'll have to send. They probably are in a box of Baby Dodds notes, I think. I was always going to try to rewrite them. When I first met Johnny Dodds about 1936, I went to Chicago and I inquired if he was playing anyplace or where he was. All I knew about him, he'd been on some of the jelly roll records…
